stem: A client taking isotretinoin reports new depressive symptoms and a marked mood change. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue isotretinoin and discuss the symptoms at the next routine visit if they persist.
options.B: Stop isotretinoin immediately and promptly contact the health care provider for further evaluation.
options.C: Reduce the isotretinoin dose and continue treatment unless suicidal thoughts or psychosis develop.
options.D: Continue isotretinoin until a mental health evaluation proves that the medication caused the mood symptoms.

rationale: Current isotretinoin labeling warns about depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, suicidality, and aggressive or violent behavior. Warnings and Precautions §5.3 instructs patients who develop depression or mood disturbance to immediately stop isotretinoin and promptly contact their health care provider; discontinuation alone may be insufficient and further evaluation may be necessary. Therefore B is correct. A and D delay the labeled action, and C substitutes an unsupported dose reduction for the instruction to stop the drug and seek prompt evaluation.
educational_objective: Teach clients who develop depression or marked mood disturbance during isotretinoin therapy to stop the medication immediately and promptly contact the health care provider for further evaluation.
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Psychiatric Disorders: assess for depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, or aggression; if these develop, instruct the patient or caregiver to immediately stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the health care provider; discontinuation may be insufficient and further evaluation may be necessary.
source_claim_supported: New depression or mood disturbance during isotretinoin treatment requires immediate discontinuation and prompt provider contact, with further evaluation as needed.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp.38-39: monitor medication adverse effects, provide client education, evaluate client response, and take action regarding medication-related harm.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — isotretinoin psychiatric adverse-effect teaching

source_original.stem: A client taking isotretinoin reports new depressive symptoms and a marked mood change. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue isotretinoin and wait until the next routine visit unless suicidal thoughts develop.
options.B: Stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber for evaluation of the new mood symptoms.
options.C: Skip the next dose only, then restart at twice the dose if the mood symptoms improve.
options.D: Assume the mood change is unrelated unless psychosis or hospitalization occurs.

source_original.rationale: Current isotretinoin labeling warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders and instructs patients who develop depression or mood disturbance to stop the drug and promptly contact the prescriber. Option B is correct. A and D delay evaluation, and C is unsafe and unsupported.
source_original.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Psychiatric Disorders: depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, suicidality and aggressive behavior are reported; patients developing depression or mood disturbance should stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber, with further evaluation as needed. DailyMed isotretinoin prescribing information revised July 2026; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, reversal, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the stem and key B. Replaced the artificial double-dose distractor and other low-quality absolute wording with plausible delays or unsupported dose-reduction strategies, while preserving the exact §5.3 instruction to stop immediately and contact the provider promptly.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed FDA labeling; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: DailyMed updated 2026-07-08; prescribing information revised 7/2026; live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item precisely follows the label's stop-now and prompt-provider-contact language and notes only that further evaluation may be necessary. No unsupported causality threshold or psychiatric severity requirement is added.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrectly delays action until a routine visit.
distractor_audit.C: Uses an unsupported dose-reduction strategy and wrongly waits for more severe psychiatric symptoms.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrectly requires proof of drug causation before following the label's safety instruction.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B follows both components of the labeled response: immediate discontinuation and prompt provider contact.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are realistic medication-management responses; the prior obviously unsafe double-dose distractor was removed.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — recognition and response to medication adverse effects.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current July 2026 label, §5.3 wording, all four options, rationale, objective, NCSBN mapping, nursing teaching scope, ambiguity and cueing. B remained uniquely correct.
